title: Bioinformatics Analysis
author: Vasso Makrantoni
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bn4bmgsn

steps.title: Set up OS and basecalling
steps.instruction: Run all data processing on Ubuntu 16.04 (xenial) and perform basecalling with Illumina Real‑Time Analysis (RTA2) software on the MiniSeq System.

steps.title: Assess raw read quality
steps.instruction: Run FastQC on the raw FASTQ files and use fastq‑screen to detect any unwanted contamination.

steps.title: Combine QC reports
steps.instruction: Aggregate all FastQC and fastq‑screen reports with MultiQC (reference [17]).

steps.title: Trim adapters and low‑quality bases
steps.instruction: Trim ChIP‑seq paired‑end reads with cutadapt, removing standard Illumina adapter sequences from the 3′ end and performing quality trimming from the 3′ end using a phred‑33 cutoff of 10.

steps.title: Discard short reads
steps.instruction: After trimming, remove any read shorter than the defined minimum length of 30 bp.

steps.title: Map reads to both genomes
steps.instruction: Map the trimmed reads separately to the S. pombe calibration genome and to the S. cerevisiae w303 experimental genome, retaining only reads that map to each reference.

steps.title: Extract SacCer‑only reads
steps.instruction: To obtain reads mapping only to SacCer W303, first map the trimmed reads to the S. pombe reference with MiniMap2 using the “-ax sr” preset for short genomic reads (reference [18]); select unmapped S. pombe reads with SAMtools using flag -F 4, convert those unmapped reads back to interleaved FASTQ, then map this FASTQ to SacCer W303; finally filter out any reads that remain unmapped (SAMtools -F 4) and remove rDNA regions on chromosome XII using BEDtools intersect (reference [20]).

steps.title: Extract S.pombe‑only reads
steps.instruction: To obtain reads mapping only to S. pombe, reverse the above workflow: map the original trimmed reads to SacCer W303, select unmapped SacCer reads with SAMtools -F 4, convert them to FASTQ, map these to the S. pombe reference, filter out any reads that remain unmapped (SAMtools -F 4), and exclude mitochondrial DNA for both genomes using SAMtools.

steps.title: Map meiotic samples to SK1
steps.instruction: For meiotic samples that used SK1 strains, map reads to the SK1 genome instead of SacCer3, following the same mapping and filtering steps described above.

steps.title: Create normalized bedGraphs and BigWigs
steps.instruction: Generate bedGraph files from the aligned BAM files with BEDtools genomeCoverageBed, normalizing to reads per million (RPM) using a custom script that incorporates SAMtools flagstat output; convert the bedGraphs to BigWig format with UCSC wigToBigWig.

steps.title: Calculate Occupancy Ratio and calibrate
steps.instruction: Use SAMtools flagstat to count reads mapping to SacCer3 W303 and to S. pombe for each sample; compute the Occupancy Ratio (OR) as Wc × IPx / Wx × IPc (W = Input, IP = ChIP, c = calibration genome S. pombe, x = experimental genome SacCer W303); apply each OR value to calibrate the ChIP bedGraphs with BEDtools genomeCoverageBed and reconvert to BigWig using UCSC wigToBigWig.

steps.title: Visualize and submit data
steps.instruction: View the final BigWig files in a genome browser such as IGV or the Ensembl genome browser; submit all BigWigs to GEO and raw reads to the SRA.
